item.title: Psychiatrists seek home-grown research to tackle Africa’s mental health crisis
item.description: … Say Nigeria’s Mental Health Act needs action, not just legislation By Chioma Obinna Nigeria and other African countries must invest in home-grown mental health research and translate policies into action to improve care for millions of people facing mental health challenges, psychiatrists have said. The experts warned that Africa’s low contribution to global mental health research was limiting the continent’s capacity to develop evidence-based responses suited to its population, while weak implementation of policies threatened to widen the gap between legislation and access to care. They spoke at the ninth International Research Conference of the Federal Neuro-Psychiatric Hospital, Yaba, Lagos, themed, “Mental Health Research at the Crossroads: Challenges, Policies and Reforms in Africa.” Professor Taiwo Lateef Sheikh, a professor of psychiatry at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, said Africa accounted for less than two per cent of global mental health research output, a situation he said underscored the urgent need to strengthen local research capacity. item.title: FG powers 2,214 homes, businesses with Kano mini-grids
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Federal Government has commissioned two solar mini-grids in Kano State, providing 2,214 electricity connections to homes and businesses in underserved communities. The projects, delivered through the Rural Electrification Agency (REA) under the Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Scale-up (DARES) programme of the Nigeria Electrification Project (NEP), are funded by the World Bank. Located in Ballagaza, Gabasawa Local Government Area, and Marayar Rogo, Warawa Local Government Area, the facilities have a combined installed capacity of 268.4 kilowatt-peak (kWp). A statement by the REA on Thursday said the Ballagaza mini-grid has a capacity of 195.2kWp, while the Marayar Rogo facility has 73.2kWp. The projects have provided 1,564 electricity connections in Ballagaza and 650 in Marayar Rogo. Speaking at the commissioning, the Minister of Power, Chief Joseph Tegbe, said the projects demonstrated the importance of investment in renewable energy and collaboration with the private sector in expanding electricity access. He said the Federal Government would continue to encourage partnerships that accelerate the delivery of reliable and sustainable electricity, particularly to rural communities. According to him, the projects would bring electricity closer to underserved populations, support small businesses and create an enabling environment for economic growth. The REA said the mini-grids were expected to support productive activities, including milling, welding, tailoring, cold storage and other commercial services, improving business operations, productivity and household incomes. Representing Kano State Governor, the Managing Director of the Kano State Rural Electricity Board, Abba Kabir Yusuf, commended the Federal Government and the REA for extending electricity infrastructure to the benefiting communities. He said improved electricity supply would support commercial activities, enhance productivity and contribute to the state’s socio-economic development. The platform hosts more than 15,000 educational resources, including lessons in English, Hausa, Igbo and Yoruba. It has recorded more than 2.5 million registered students and nearly 100,000 registered teachers. The initiative, introduced in Nigeria during the COVID-19 pandemic when school closures disrupted learning nationwide, is now hosted by the Federal Ministry of Education as part of efforts to expand access to educational resources. Through the partnership, Airtel provides zero-rated access to the Nigeria Learning Passport, the ministry’s Inspire and Ignite platforms, the Digital National Education Management Information System and the Youth Agency Marketplace, also known as YOMA. The arrangement allows users to access the designated platforms without incurring mobile data charges, addressing one of the major obstacles to digital learning for families with limited resources. Head of Programmes at the Airtel Africa Foundation, Esi Asare Prah, said digital inclusion in education was central to preparing young Africans for an increasingly technology-driven world. “One of the biggest missions for the foundation is driving faster digital inclusion in education to improve learning outcomes,” Prah said. “For Airtel as an organisation, digital inclusion is a major priority. We want to ensure that young people across Africa are equipped for the future.” She said the visit demonstrated how access to digital resources could help young learners, particularly girls, gain confidence in technology and develop practical skills. “It was wonderful to see young girls taking full advantage of the opportunity afforded by the zero-rated Learning Passport,” she said. “Because they can learn free of charge, they are able to absorb information and, within minutes, develop content from what they’ve learned.” Prah said the Airtel Africa Foundation was committed to strengthening digital infrastructure, expanding access in underserved rural communities, empowering marginalised groups and promoting long-term educational equity. She added that young people across Nigeria with an Airtel connection could access the Nigeria Learning Passport free of charge. For students, the benefits extend beyond lessons delivered in school. The Head Girl of Government Senior College, Tosin Adeola, said the platform had improved students’ academic performance and study habits by allowing them to revisit lessons and review difficult topics at home. She thanked UNICEF and Airtel for providing the opportunity, saying students were determined to make effective use of the platform. Airtel Africa Foundation committee member, Spillane, said connectivity could transform education when it enabled students to access quality learning materials and teachers to use digital tools effectively. “Connectivity brings transformative opportunities when it helps students access quality digital learning and enables teachers to use digital tools effectively, as we’ve seen demonstrated so ably here in Nigeria,” he said. “Working with UNICEF and governments, we will continue to connect schools, remove data-cost barriers through zero-rated learning platforms and support teachers across the continent.” The Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Sa’idu Ahmad, said collaboration among government, development partners and telecommunications providers was necessary to improve learning outcomes and ensure that digital education reached children regardless of their location. “Transforming education in Nigeria requires strong partnerships aligned with government priorities and learners’ needs,” Ahmad said. “We must strengthen teachers’ capacity, expand access to quality digital content, protect children online and ensure digital learning reaches every child, wherever they live.” In Abuja, the delegation also met with the Office of the Vice President and the Federal Ministry of Education to discuss reliable connectivity, quality learning content, teacher training, inclusive digital design, stronger education data systems, child online safety and sustainable financing. The partners reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening these areas to improve learning outcomes and expand access to digital education. Across 13 African countries, the five-year Airtel Africa-UNICEF partnership has connected more than 3,000 schools, provided zero-rated access to more than 60 learning platforms and reached over 2.5 million children. The partners said continued collaboration with governments would be critical to expanding the initiative and ensuring that more children and young people, particularly those in underserved communities, could benefit from digital learning and the opportunities it creates. item.description: By Dayo Johnson The family of the late Afenifere Leader, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, has announced his burial plans, showing that his remains will be buried on December 17, 2026. item.title: Judge gives Trump Dec. 11 deadline to testify in BBC lawsuit
item.description: A US judge on Thursday issued President Donald Trump a December 11 deadline to testify under oath in his $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC. Judge Enjolique Lett in Miami gave the order in response to complaints by the British broadcaster that Trump has refused to sit for a deposition, including canceling a previously agreed date of October 16. If Trump fails to attend the deposition by then, he risks sanctions, including dismissal of his lawsuit, the court said. Trump has accused the BBC of deceptively editing its documentary “Trump: A Second Chance” to make it seem as if he was inciting violence when he told supporters to march on the US Capitol on January 6, 2021, after losing the presidential election. The crowd proceeded to storm Congress in an attempt to stop the formal certification of Democrat Joe Biden’s victory. While the BBC has apologized for the incident, which prompted the resignation of multiple senior executives, the broadcaster has denied it caused Trump any real injury and moved for the case to be dismissed. Trump filed his suit against the BBC in December 2025 and is seeking at least $5 billion on each of two counts. Charles Tobin, a lawyer for the BBC, said in court that Trump had no real excuse not to testify and that on October 16, he had only been campaigning, “participating in party politics.” “No plaintiff is above the law,” Tobin said. In a court filing Wednesday, Trump’s legal team argued that he was not seeking to avoid a deposition but had been constrained by “matters of national importance.” The lawyers said Trump would be able to give a deposition between January 11 and 22. Trump has made attacks on the media a signature of his two presidential terms, insulting reporters who ask questions he doesn’t like and seeking to ban outlets airing critical reports from the White House. Most recently, the administration has plunged into a legal dispute with CNN, MSNOW and Politico over attempts to bar them from the White House. With his approval ratings in the low 30 percent range and polls showing his Republican Party likely to lose control of the House of Representatives in the November 3 midterm elections, Trump faces increasing headwinds as he approaches his final years in power. item.title: N10bn untouched – APC accuses Atiku of politicising Ebola response
item.description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused former Vice-President, Atiku Abubakar, of politicising Nigeria’s Ebola response, insisting that approved emergency funds remain untouched. The council’s spokesperson, Mr Dele Alake, said this in a statement issued on Thursday in Abuja. Alake said President Bola Tinubu approved N10 billion for the Ebola emergency in June, but relevant agencies deployed other available resources. “On accountability, the Atiku camp should note that the N10 billion the President approved for the Ebola emergency in June remains untouched,” he said. He said the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) and other agencies strengthened surveillance at entry points. According to him, the surveillance network alerted the government to the index case and facilitated contact tracing for 44 contacts. The council commended the agencies for their contributions to monitoring the Ebola threat and supporting the public health response. It also criticised Atiku’s reference linking President Tinubu’s name to Ebola, saying it risked turning a serious health concern into political ridicule. “We believe linking and rhyming President Bola Tinubu’s name to Ebola only risks turning a serious health concern into a vehicle to ridicule the President,” Alake said. The council also defended the handling of the infected Nigerian’s detection, citing the virus’s incubation period and the timing of symptoms. “For anyone infected with the virus, the incubation period ranges from two to 21 days, with symptoms typically appearing eight to 10 days after exposure. “An infected person cannot spread or transmit Ebola to others until they actively develop symptoms,” he said. Alake urged opposition politicians to support health authorities rather than criticise the government’s response to the public health threat. “A responsible opposition will applaud the Task Force for being responsive. But the Atiku camp always goes for cheap shots at the government,” he said. The council also rejected Atiku’s allegation that a ministerial briefing was intended to discourage Nigerians from attending campaign rallies or voting. Alake described the allegation as speculative, adding that the briefing instead urged Nigerians to comply with protocols announced by the task force. He called on Atiku and his supporters to avoid politicising public health concerns, urging Nigerians to shun rumours and follow health authorities’ guidance. “We advise Atiku Abubakar and his hirelings to avoid politicising public health issues,” he said. The council said protecting Nigerians from the deadly disease should remain the priority. item.title: Tinubu names former DSS DG Bichi NISS board chairman
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has appointed former Director-General of the Department of State Services, Yusuf Bichi, as Chairman of the Governing Board of the National Institute for Security Studies. The appointment was announced in a statement issued on Thursday by the institute’s Director of Coordination and Liaison, Lilian Omo-Odigwe, and published through the DSS’s X account. According to the statement, Bichi’s appointment followed a recommendation by the incumbent DSS Director-General, Oluwatosin Ajayi. “The Commander-In-Chief of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, President Bola Tinubu, GCFR, has approved the appointment of Y. M. Bichi, CFR, FWC, the immediate past Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), as Chairman of the Governing Board of the National Institute for Security Studies (NISS), Lower Usuma Dam, Abuja.” The statement added, “Bichi’s appointment was approved by President Tinubu based on the recommendation of the current DG-DSS, Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi.” Bichi’s appointment took effect on Thursday, October 22, 2026, and will run for an initial four-year term. “His appointment is for an initial four-year term, effective 22nd October, 2026, in accordance with Section 4 of the National Institute for Security Studies (Establishment) Act, 2019,” the statement said. He succeeds A.A. Gadzama as chairman of the institute’s governing board. Bichi previously led the DSS before handing over to Ajayi in August 2024. “Bichi, who will succeed A.A. item.title: We sought Aso Rock venue because APC uses it too – Sowore
item.description: Presidential candidate of the African Action Congress, Omoyele Sowore, has defended his party’s request to hold the inauguration of its 2027 Presidential Campaign Council at the Presidential Villa in Abuja, arguing that opposition parties should enjoy the same access as the ruling All Progressives Congress. Sowore made the remarks on Thursday at an event organised by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria, explaining that the request was prompted by the APC’s use of the facility for political activities. The AAC had written to President Bola Tinubu seeking approval to inaugurate its Presidential Campaign Council at the Villa ahead of the 2027 general elections. “We asked to use Aso Rock because the APC uses Aso Rock to do political party events. So we are saying, as a matter of right, since Aso Rock is our own, other political parties must be granted the opportunity to use Aso Rock the way APC uses Aso Rock,” Sowore said. In addition to the venue, the party requested food, drinks and other logistical arrangements for attendees at the proposed inauguration scheduled for November 11, 2026. A letter dated October 21 and signed by the AAC National Secretary, Oshiokhai Ikpeminioghena, stated that the request was anchored on multiparty democracy, political inclusiveness and equal treatment of political parties. The party maintained that approving the request would affirm the Presidency’s commitment to fairness and demonstrate that public institutions were available to all Nigerians, irrespective of political affiliation. The request triggered a disagreement between Sowore and the APC National Secretary, Ajibola Basiru, who criticised the AAC candidate and questioned the party’s electoral strength. item.title: Trump slams LeBron James for national anthem actions
item.description: US President Donald Trump lashed out at NBA superstar LeBron James on Thursday for what he called disrespectful behaviour during the playing of the national anthem. Trump posted a video of the basketball legend doing apparent warm-up movements while lined up with his Philadelphia 76ers teammates. “While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country! I said right from the beginning that he’s no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social network. “LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!” he wrote. The video used by Trump had an internal caption that read: “LeBron working on his golf swing pregame.” It showed him doing lateral swing motions and basketball shooting movements. It was not immediately clear when the video was filmed. There was no immediate reaction from James, 41, who is entering a record-extending 24th NBA season with his fourth team, the 76ers. Trump has been critical of athletes before — particularly Black athletes — for their behaviour during the playing of the US national anthem before games. During his first term, Trump singled out NFL star Colin Kaepernick for his decision to kneel during the “Star-Spangled Banner” to protest racial injustice and police brutality. item.title: 2027 Election: Even Tinubu Knows Atiku Is The Best Candidate – Momodu
item.description: The Deputy Director-General, Media and Communications of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign, Dele Momodu, has described the party’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, as the best candidate for the 2027 election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Momodu said Atiku had been the most deliberate and focused candidate since he first sought the presidency in 1993. The ADC chieftain claimed that President Bola Tinubu, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the All Progressives Congress (APC), also knows that the former vice president is better suited for the job. “When I say he (Atiku) is the best, it is a statement of fact and even President Bola Tinubu himself knows that,” Momodu said. “That is why at a time, he invited him and they joined hands for Atiku to run in the past.” ﻿ Comparing the credentials of the three major presidential candidates, Momodu said Tinubu’s strongest credential was his tenure as governor of Lagos State, while Atiku’s was his experience as vice president and Peter Obi’s as governor of Anambra State. He argued that Tinubu had underestimated the differences between governing Lagos and leading Nigeria. “So, if you look at the three mainstream candidates today, the APC candidate Bola Tinubu, the ADC candidate Atiku Abubakar and the NDC candidate Peter Obi, you can judge for yourself. Bola Tinubu came, his best credential was being the former governor of Lagos State; Atiku came, his best credential was being the former vice president of Nigeria; Peter Obi came, his best credential was being the governor of Anambra State. “So, if you judge for yourself, you will know that perhaps what has happened to President Tinubu is the fact that when he got to the Presidency, he assumed that Nigeria was Lagos and he soon discovered that Nigeria is different from Lagos and that is why he’s had total commotional confusion and his guys are running all over the places throwing money around.” Momodu also accused the Tinubu administration of failing to be sincere with Nigerians, alleging that officials around the President were more concerned with telling him what he wanted to hear than confronting him with the realities facing the country. “What is lacking in this government is that sincerity. Everything is about one man. The people who are running our economy today have to tell Nigerians only what they think the president wants to hear. They are not telling him the truth, and when tomorrow comes, he will realise it,” he added. item.title: Obasanjo’s son joins Tinubu Must Stay Movement
item.description: Olujonwo Obasanjo, son of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, has joined the Tinubu Must Stay Movement, pledging to promote policy continuity and explain President Bola Tinubu’s reforms. He announced his decision at a news conference in Abuja on Thursday, where the leadership of the Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation (TMS) welcomed him. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that TMS is a political advocacy platform promoting policy continuity, sustainable governance and public understanding of Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda. Olujonwo said his decision was shaped by his political experience, understanding of Nigeria’s reform history and belief in sustaining government policies across administrations. “I’ve been in the APC since 2014. I was there when my father hosted late President Muhammadu Buhari and President Bola Tinubu to form the movement. I’m not new to the party,” he said. He said inadequate communication about the Tinubu administration’s policies had created opportunities for misinformation and misinterpretation among Nigerians. “There’s a lot of noise out there, and people are distorting what’s going on. ASUU has had no strikes. Students now have access to education loans. “Nigeria has become a massive construction site and an investors’ haven again. These are things we need to promote,” he said. Olujonwo said communicating government policies required explaining their objectives, implementation processes and implications for citizens rather than relying solely on political slogans. Abdullahi said Olujonwo’s family background gave him an understanding of economic reforms and their implications for national development. “You grew up in a family that led the second wave of reforms in Nigeria. Telecommunications liberalisation and banking reforms — these laid a solid foundation. “Being raised in that family, you understand what reforms mean,” he added. item.title: UEL: Juventus denied at the death, Sunderland make point in Poland
item.description: Bayer Leverkusen made it three straight wins in the Europa League with a Jonas Hofmann double earning a 2-0 away win at OFI Crete as both Juventus and Sunderland lost ground in Thursday’s third matchday. The once mighty Hungarian side Ferencvaros kept pace with Leverkusen on nine points thumping Portuguese outfit Torreense 4-1, while Belgium’s Union Saint-Gilloise won 4-0 against Israeli outfit Hapoel Be’er Sheva. Saint-Gilloise, Sunderland and Juve all have seven points from three games. Juventus thought they had come from behind to beat French side Rennes but had their late ‘winner’ ruled out for a marginal offside. Zeki Celik put Juve ahead after five minutes only for a poor clearance 10 minutes later allowing Musa Al-Taamari to poke home an equaliser. Jut before the break Boulaye Dia put the visitors ahead. Juventus made it 2-2 thanks to a handball and a spot-kick transformed by Nick Woltemade before VAR provided the biggest talking point, disallowing Jhon Lucumi’s 88th minute strike. Clad in a new all-pink kit, Sunderland were left kicking themselves after a 1-1 draw in Poland. The Blacks Cats took a second-half lead in Poznan thanks to Timur Tutierov and dominated the game without being able to close out the win. With two home games remaining, however, the second round still beckons for Regis Le Bris’ men. In the Conference League, former Liverpool striker Mohamed Salah opened the scoring from the penalty spot in Trabzonspor’s 2-0 win over Scottish side Hearts. item.title: Tinubu appoints Yusuf Bichi chairman of NISS governing board
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has appointed Y. M. Bichi, the immediate past Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), as chairman of the Governing Board of the National Institute for Security Studies (NISS), Abuja. Bichi’s appointment, based on the recommendation of the current DSS Director-General, Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi, takes effect from October 22, 2026, for an initial four-year term. According to a statement by the Director of Coordination and Liaison, NISS, Lilian Omo-Odigwe, the appointment was made in accordance with Section 4 of the National Institute for Security Studies (Establishment) Act, 2019. Bichi succeeds A. A. Gadzama on the governing board. He handed over leadership of the DSS to the incumbent director-general in August 2024. Before his appointment as DSS director-general, Bichi began his career in the Security Division of the Kano State Cabinet Office before his transfer of service in 1984. His appointment brings experience in intelligence, security administration, operational leadership and institutional training to the governance of the institute. He said the trend limits access to essential medical services and increases the workload on available health personnel. item.title: 2027: APC will campaign on achievements, not insults – Gov. Yusuf
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf Kano State Governor Abba Yusuf has promised that the All Progressives Congress (APC) will focus on issues, achievements and plans rather than personal attacks in its campaign ahead of the 2027 general election. Yusuf gave the assurance on Thursday during the inauguration of the APC 2027 presidential and gubernatorial campaign council management team in Kano. He said the party would explain its achievements to voters, present its plans for the future and listen to the needs of the people. “We are going to campaign based on what the APC leaders have done, not campaign full of insults,” the governor said. Yusuf said members of the campaign council were selected based on their capacity to carry out the responsibilities assigned to them. He urged them to work hard to ensure that the APC secured more votes in Kano than in any other state during the 2027 elections. “Kano should garner a lot of votes for President Tinubu. The number of votes the APC gets in Kano should be the highest in the country. This is possible if you go out and campaign as required,” he said. The governor described the council members as representatives of the party who must work towards securing victory for the APC and President Bola Tinubu. “The members of this council are APC soldiers, and I urge you to carry out your responsibilities with commitment and work towards the party’s victory,” Yusuf said. He also urged them not to be intimidated by opposition parties or allow fear to affect their campaign activities, insisting that the APC had established itself in the state. Yusuf appealed to party members and supporters whose names were not included in the initial campaign council list not to feel disappointed, explaining that additional lists and subcommittees would be announced. He called on party members to remain committed and work together to mobilise support for the APC ahead of the 2027 elections. Among the key appointments, Abdullahi Tijjani Muhammad Gwarzo was named Director-General of the campaign council, while Hon. Bala Muhammad Gwagwarwa will serve as First Deputy Director-General. Dr. Yunusa Adamu Dangwani was appointed Deputy Director-General for Kano South, while Dr. Ali Haruna Abubakar Makoda and Senator Abdussalam Abdulkarim Zaura will serve as Deputy Directors-General for Kano North and Kano Central, respectively. Dr. Mariya Mahmoud Bunkure was also named Assistant Director-General for Women Affairs, while Hon. Garba Yusuf Abubakar will serve as Assistant Director-General for Operations, among other appointments. item.title: Stop announcing how much your movie made at the cinema — Filmmaker Biodun Stephen tells colleagues
item.description: Nollywood filmmaker Biodun Stephen has urged colleagues to stop announcing cinema earnings, warning that the practice puts unnecessary pressure on other filmmakers and creates a narrow definition of success in the industry. The claims that the State Government sanctioned acts of violence, abduction, or illegal electricity connections are reckless, unfounded, and unacceptable.” Addressing the allegations surrounding the reported attack on JED workers, the government questioned the evidence linking it to the incident, arguing that the distribution company had not provided verifiable details to substantiate its claims. According to the statement: “JED Plc’s own use of the word ‘allegedly’ confirms that it has no evidence linking the Government to the incident of October 21, 2026. No names, identities, or credible references were provided. The Government categorically rejects this insinuation.” On the dispute over electricity supply to Government House, the state government said issues concerning transformer energisation and alleged metering irregularities should be handled through the appropriate regulatory and judicial channels. It stated, “Issues of transformer energization and metering irregularities are regulatory matters. They must be addressed before the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) and, where necessary, the courts, not through inflammatory press releases. “Assertions of abduction, assault, and injuries remain unsubstantiated. The Government does not condone violence and demands that impartial, evidence-based, and transparent investigations be carried out by security operatives,” the statement added. It challenged the distribution company to produce documentary evidence of its alleged previous communications with the state government over the dispute. “The company has failed to produce records of its alleged ‘several communications’ with the Government. The State challenges JED Plc to publish such correspondence if it exists,” the statement said. Insisting that electricity distribution companies must comply with the same regulatory requirements and safety standards applicable to their customers, the government said JED must also be held accountable for its operations. The statement added: “JED Plc itself acknowledges that interventions must comply with regulatory requirements and safety standards. Consequently, the government demanded the immediate withdrawal of what it described as the insinuation that it sanctioned violence, a retraction of the allegation that it engaged in meter bypassing or illegal electricity connections, and a formal apology to the government and the people of Benue State. It warned that it would consider legal action if JED persisted in disseminating what it described as false information. “The Government remains committed to the rule of law, the protection of lives and property, and constructive engagement with stakeholders in the electricity sector. However, it will not hesitate to pursue legal remedies should JED Plc persist in disseminating falsehoods,” the statement said. The government added that the people of Benue State deserved reliable electricity supply, respectful treatment and accountability rather than what it termed reckless allegations. As of the time of filing this report, the dispute had resulted in a shutdown of electricity supply to Makurdi, with the workers insisting that they would not resume operations until the matter was resolved with their union.
